original_question: To what extent are Theorem 13.1 and Conjecture 13.2 valid if one replaces Q̄ with a number field K?
target_in_paper: Question 13.4 in Section 13 (Orbits of Rational Maps), immediately following Theorem 13.1 and Conjecture 13.2: the paper asks to what extent those two statements remain true when Q̄ is replaced by a number field K.
correct_elements: Your draft has the right target and essentially matches the paper's own Question 13.4. It correctly ties together exactly the two nearby statements in Section 13, keeps the scope narrow, and focuses on the intended field-of-definition issue Q̄ versus a number field K rather than drifting to the broader arbitrary-variety generalization in Section 13.1.
missing_details: It is not stand-alone unless Theorem 13.1 is spelled out: f is a dominant rational self-map of P^N, and the conclusion is that wandering points in P^N(Q̄)_f are Zariski dense in P^N.
It should define P^N(K)_f (or P^N(Q̄)_f): the set of points whose entire forward orbit is well-defined, i.e. every iterate avoids the indeterminacy locus of f.
It should define 'wandering': a point whose forward orbit is infinite.
It should spell out that Conjecture 13.2 is not about arbitrary rational maps on P^N, but about polynomial morphisms f = (f_1,...,f_N): A^N -> A^N.
It should include the coordinate description in Conjecture 13.2: f_i are polynomials in x_1,...,x_N with coefficients in the ground field.
It should include the exact obstruction in Conjecture 13.2: there is no nonconstant rational function g with g∘f = g.

For the K-version, it should say explicitly whether the invariant-function condition is interpreted over K or over an algebraic closure Kbar; the nearby general formulation Conjecture 13.5 shows that the natural geometric version uses Kbar.
It should state the exact conclusion of the K-analogue of Conjecture 13.2: existence of a K-rational point whose forward orbit is Zariski dense in A^N.
It should make explicit that the maps themselves should be defined over K in the K-rational variant; otherwise 'replace Q̄ by K' is ambiguous.
It should preserve the paper's P^N/A^N distinction and not broaden the question to the arbitrary quasi-projective-variety setting of Conjecture 13.5.
refined_question: Let K be a number field. If one asks for K-rational points rather than Q̄-rational points in Section 13, are the following K-rational analogues of Theorem 13.1 and Conjecture 13.2 true? (1) For every dominant rational map f: P^N dashrightarrow P^N defined over K, is the set of wandering points in P^N(K)_f, meaning K-points whose full forward orbit avoids the indeterminacy locus and is infinite, Zariski dense in P^N? (2) For every polynomial morphism f = (f_1,...,f_N): A^N -> A^N defined over K, with f_i in K[x_1,...,x_N], and with no nonconstant invariant rational function g in Kbar(x_1,...,x_N) satisfying g∘f = g, does there exist a point P in A^N(K) whose forward orbit O_f(P) is Zariski dense in A^N?
justification: The nearest official formulation is not a reformulation in the introduction but the explicit open problem Question 13.4 in Section 13. Your draft is already very close to that exact question. To make it fully stand-alone and paper-faithful, one must unpack the precise statements of Theorem 13.1 and Conjecture 13.2, define the notation P^N(K)_f and 'wandering', and preserve the asymmetry between the two statements: Theorem 13.1 concerns dominant rational self-maps of P^N, whereas Conjecture 13.2 concerns polynomial self-maps of A^N with no invariant rational fibration. I did not broaden the question to the arbitrary-variety version in Conjecture 13.5, because the paper itself poses Question 13.4 specifically for Theorem 13.1 and Conjecture 13.2 before giving that wider generalization.
